        <section class="content article-content mb-6" itemprop="articleBody">
          <p>Follow this article to receive email notifications when Optimizely Content Management System (SaaS) features are available for 2026.</p><div class="note">Optimizely CMS (SaaS) release notes provide information on the latest innovations. To ensure stability and high quality, Optimizely rolls out features progressively in <a href="https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/overview-saas#platform-updates" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">ring deployments</a>, so you may see announcements for features before they are universally available.</div><h2 id="h_01KTY9FP9WFYFTFAWWW4AWZ66Y">July 7<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KTY9FP9WFYFTFAWWW4AWZ66Y"></a></h2><!-- JS SDK 2.1.0 - added by Katy --><details><summary><h4 style="display: inline;" id="h_RELEASE_SUMMARY_ID">Richer content modeling and tooling in the JavaScript SDK</h4></summary><p><a href="https://github.com/episerver/content-js-sdk/releases" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">@optimizely/cms-sdk</a></p>
<ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e238e89280803bccd14a2c772225c15d2">Queries now return all base type properties, so you can access more content data without extra configuration.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eab25f5569e0014539e0dbd1df5d2339f">Locale support now extends to <code>ContentType</code> and <code>RICHTEXT_PRESET</code>, which makes multilingual experiences easier to build.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e3aea1d035411f5cc7d2dc843f3f9dbbb">
<code>OptimizelyComposition</code> now handles section fragments automatically, so you write less boilerplate when working with compositions.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eee44698553218f5d93ea5cf6a03ef55d">Content type contracts now support allowed and restricted types, fragment generation, and a component fallback. A single <code>expandContracts</code> boolean controls contract expansion, replacing the more complex <code>maxContractExpansionLimit</code>.</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="https://github.com/episerver/content-js-sdk/releases" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">@optimizely/cms-cli</a></p>
<ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ecc7911bbe8f76d30a40b6f1623d454f9">Code generation now supports circular and self-referenced content types, so you can model more complex content relationships.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ea576a006ecf791c4b12a63417637d07c">The <code>pull</code> command now preserves editor settings on RichText properties, keeping richer authoring configuration in your codebase.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ef074c0a4b4fabb756cc36fb843bf1e70">The CLI now supports self-signed certificates, so you can run it against local or internal CMS environments more easily.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e3dfadaee0aa8a2e66276db8de55922a5">The <code>pull</code> command now shows clearer progress messaging, giving you better visibility into what it is doing as it runs.</li>
</ul></details><h2 id="h_01KWYR05APT8NS6MJX926M92AG">July 3<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KWYR05APT8NS6MJX926M92AG"></a></h2><!-- SaaS-v2026.05.18.0255 and SaaS-v2026.06.17.1354 - added by Katy --><details><summary><h4 style="display: inline;" id="h_01KTWJ2B3C4D5E6F7G8H9J0K1L">Bug fixes</h4></summary><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ed2bcfe20a0ee6280c4c725a705787bd2">
<a href="https://world.optimizely.com/support/bug-list/bug/CMS-53444" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">CMS-53444</a> – Fixed an issue where copying, exporting, or saving an experience as a blueprint produced empty rows, columns, and elements in the copy when the original experience had been translated into another language.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="efb0fe07465702d9c5b2b17997863ee09">
<a href="https://world.optimizely.com/support/bug-list/bug/CMS-53567" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">CMS-53567</a> – Fixed an issue where importing an experience with the <strong>Update existing content items with matching ID</strong> option could leave duplicate block data behind, causing blocks to show the wrong type or field values.</li>
</ul></details><h2 id="h_01KWFA86TNHT7BKP1SBHBHEDWY">June 23<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KWFA86TNHT7BKP1SBHBHEDWY"></a></h2><!-- SaaS-v2026.06.17.1353 - added by Katy --><details><summary><h4 style="display: inline;" id="h_01KVT5H7DDMEKGAVPEC6DR8MNB">Bug fixes</h4></summary><ul><li data-list-item-id="e955dc5ed189c0635c378aa86cbe7628e">
<a href="https://world.optimizely.com/support/bug-list/bug/CMS-53365" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">CMS-53365</a> – Fixed an issue where expanding a page tree node with a large number of child items failed to load when those items contained large amounts of property data.</li></ul></details><h2 id="h_01KVT5FA0KPA11Y9XG22R2C5Q4">June 18<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KVT5FA0KPA11Y9XG22R2C5Q4"></a></h2><!-- Not part of a specific release package - added by Katy --><details><summary><h4 style="display: inline;" id="h_01EOLPREVIEW3CMSRESTAPIEXPERIMENTAL">Preview3 CMS REST API reaches end-of-life on August 1, 2026</h4></summary><p><strong>Action required: Migrate Preview3 API integrations to CMS REST API v1 before August 1, 2026</strong></p>
<p>If your CMS (SaaS) applications use the Preview3 CMS REST API endpoints, migrate to CMS REST API v1 before August 1, 2026. On August 1, 2026, Optimizely retires the Preview3 endpoints and begins disabling access. Applications that rely on Preview3 after this date may experience failed requests and service interruptions.</p>
<p><strong>Who is affected</strong> – This change affects CMS (SaaS) integrations that make requests to Preview3 endpoints (typically URLs containing <code>/preview3/</code>). If your applications already use CMS REST API v1, no action is required. Optimizely has maintained support for both versions since CMS REST API v1 was released in May 2026 and provides a <a href="https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/reference/migrate-content-api-preview3-to-v1" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">migration guide</a> to support the transition.</p>
<p><strong>What is changing</strong> – With the general availability of CMS REST API v1 on May 5, 2026, the Preview3 APIs entered a deprecation phase and are now approaching end-of-life.</p>
<ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e547b841f9c9c0fc8cb14fa2aa4412ab2">Preview3 support ends August 1, 2026.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e99b1af93c58fab1e0830780567dbf1d1">Preview3 was released as an experimental API and was not recommended for production workloads.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e024e5d46b144c5a17ba7c512df9a1022">CMS REST API v1 provides the same core capabilities through stabilized, production-ready endpoints.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e87deb4d3ea99a7bf32cc80870460db1d">Mixing Preview3 and v1 endpoints is supported until the August 1, 2026 retirement date.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e33ab2e14f8be827cd55dfc7be9ef754b">Preview3 receives no further fixes, enhancements, or support updates. Ongoing investment focuses on v1 and future releases.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Breaking changes</strong> – The transition from Preview3 to v1 introduced some breaking changes. <p><strong>Why Preview3 is being retired</strong> – Maintaining multiple API versions increases complexity for both customers and Optimizely. </ul>
<p>If you have questions about your migration strategy or encounter challenges during the transition, contact Optimizely.</p></details><h2 id="h_01KVDYAJAM5KM9NCEV63FCRJ0C">June 10<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KVDYAJAM5KM9NCEV63FCRJ0C"></a></h2><!-- Not part of a specific release package - added by Nayeem --><details><summary><h4 style="display: inline;" id="h_01JWVP3KQRT5MN8XB2YC4ZD6AE">Agent Visibility Analytics dashboard</h4></summary><p>Released the <a href="https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/45787354895757-Agent-Visibility-Analytics-dashboard-in-Optimizely-Analytics" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Agent Visibility Analytics dashboard in Optimizely Analytics</a>, which shows how AI platforms interact with your website so you can refine your content strategy for AI optimization. 2026 CMS (SaaS) release notes – Support Help Center                   

[Skip to main content](#page-container)

Follow this article to receive email notifications when Optimizely Content Management System (SaaS) features are available for 2026.

Optimizely CMS (SaaS) release notes provide information on the latest innovations. To ensure stability and high quality, Optimizely rolls out features progressively in [ring deployments](https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/overview-saas#platform-updates), so you may see announcements for features before they are universally available.

## July 7[](#h_01KTY9FP9WFYFTFAWWW4AWZ66Y)

#### Richer content modeling and tooling in the JavaScript SDK

[@optimizely/cms-sdk](https://github.com/episerver/content-js-sdk/releases)

*   Queries now return all base type properties, so you can access more content data without extra configuration.
*   Locale support now extends to `ContentType` and `RICHTEXT_PRESET`, which makes multilingual experiences easier to build.
*   `OptimizelyComposition` now handles section fragments automatically, so you write less boilerplate when working with compositions.
*   Content type contracts now support allowed and restricted types, fragment generation, and a component fallback. A single `expandContracts` boolean controls contract expansion, replacing the more complex `maxContractExpansionLimit`.

[@optimizely/cms-cli](https://github.com/episerver/content-js-sdk/releases)

*   Code generation now supports circular and self-referenced content types, so you can model more complex content relationships.
*   The `pull` command now preserves editor settings on RichText properties, keeping richer authoring configuration in your codebase.
*   The CLI now supports self-signed certificates, so you can run it against local or internal CMS environments more easily.
*   The `pull` command now shows clearer progress messaging, giving you better visibility into what it is doing as it runs.

## July 3[](#h_01KWYR05APT8NS6MJX926M92AG)

#### Bug fixes

*   [CMS-53444](https://world.optimizely.com/support/bug-list/bug/CMS-53444) – Fixed an issue where copying, exporting, or saving an experience as a blueprint produced empty rows, columns, and elements in the copy when the original experience had been translated into another language.
*   [CMS-53567](https://world.optimizely.com/support/bug-list/bug/CMS-53567) – Fixed an issue where importing an experience with the **Update existing content items with matching ID** option could leave duplicate block data behind, causing blocks to show the wrong type or field values.

## June 23[](#h_01KWFA86TNHT7BKP1SBHBHEDWY)

#### Bug fixes

*   [CMS-53365](https://world.optimizely.com/support/bug-list/bug/CMS-53365) – Fixed an issue where expanding a page tree node with a large number of child items failed to load when those items contained large amounts of property data.

## June 18[](#h_01KVT5FA0KPA11Y9XG22R2C5Q4)

#### Preview3 CMS REST API reaches end-of-life on August 1, 2026

**Action required: Migrate Preview3 API integrations to CMS REST API v1 before August 1, 2026**

If your CMS (SaaS) applications use the Preview3 CMS REST API endpoints, migrate to CMS REST API v1 before August 1, 2026. On August 1, 2026, Optimizely retires the Preview3 endpoints and begins disabling access. Applications that rely on Preview3 after this date may experience failed requests and service interruptions.

**Who is affected** – This change affects CMS (SaaS) integrations that make requests to Preview3 endpoints (typically URLs containing `/preview3/`). If your applications already use CMS REST API v1, no action is required. Optimizely has maintained support for both versions since CMS REST API v1 was released in May 2026 and provides a [migration guide](https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/reference/migrate-content-api-preview3-to-v1) to support the transition.

**What is changing** – With the general availability of CMS REST API v1 on May 5, 2026, the Preview3 APIs entered a deprecation phase and are now approaching end-of-life.

*   Preview3 support ends August 1, 2026.
*   Preview3 was released as an experimental API and was not recommended for production workloads.
*   CMS REST API v1 provides the same core capabilities through stabilized, production-ready endpoints.
*   Mixing Preview3 and v1 endpoints is supported until the August 1, 2026 retirement date.
*   Preview3 receives no further fixes, enhancements, or support updates. Ongoing investment focuses on v1 and future releases.

**Breaking changes** – The transition from Preview3 to v1 introduced some breaking changes. Before migrating, review the [migration guide](https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/reference/migrate-content-api-preview3-to-v1) and the [experimental APIs documentation](https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/reference/migrate-content-api-preview3-to-v1) for detailed guidance and the recommended migration approach.

**Why Preview3 is being retired** – Maintaining multiple API versions increases complexity for both customers and Optimizely. Because v1 has been generally available for several months and provides a stable, supported alternative, retiring Preview3 lets Optimizely focus on higher reliability, better performance, and faster innovation across the platform.

**How to stay informed** – For future API lifecycle and platform updates, subscribe to the following channels, which are typically the first to communicate deprecations, support timelines, and migration guidance:

*   CMS release notes
*   Optimizely Slack Community
*   [Optimizely Developer Blog Community](https://world.optimizely.com)

If you have questions about your migration strategy or encounter challenges during the transition, contact Optimizely.

## June 10[](#h_01KVDYAJAM5KM9NCEV63FCRJ0C)

#### Agent Visibility Analytics dashboard

Released the [Agent Visibility Analytics dashboard in Optimizely Analytics](https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/45787354895757-Agent-Visibility-Analytics-dashboard-in-Optimizely-Analytics), which shows how AI platforms interact with your website so you can refine your content strategy for AI optimization. It draws on content delivery network (CDN) log data and Opal-generated insights, letting you monitor AI traffic patterns, see which AI platforms visit most often, and identify which pages attract the most AI attention.

## June 8[](#h_01KTVJ569R9V6ZJJKWGTV5PA1G)

#### Select multiple items from the Content Manager picker

The Content Manager picker now supports multi-select when [adding content to a **Content Reference List** property](https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/manage-content-with-content-manager#use-content-in-visual-builder). Select as many items as you need in a single session, then confirm to add them all at once.

If a property has a configured item limit, the picker shows your running count and alerts you as you approach the minimum or maximum, keeping you informed without blocking your selection. Multi-select works across all content sources in the picker, including CMS content, DAM assets, and Commerce products.

#### Bug fixes

*   [CMS-38305](https://world.optimizely.com/support/bug-list/bug/CMS-38305) – Fixed an issue where switching between On-Page Editing, Visual Builder, and Preview caused "Not authorized" errors after an authentication token expired.
*   [CMS-48545](https://world.optimizely.com/support/bug-list/bug/CMS-48545) – Fixed an issue where saving a media content type with an invalid file extension showed an empty error message instead of a descriptive one.
*   [CMS-49112](https://world.optimizely.com/support/bug-list/bug/CMS-49112) – Fixed an issue where helper text tooltips were not shown for block properties when editing content in Visual Builder.
*   [CMS-49360](https://world.optimizely.com/support/bug-list/bug/CMS-49360) – Fixed an issue where posting a manifest failed when two content types referenced each other in a circular `mayContainTypes` configuration.
*   [CMS-49431](https://world.optimizely.com/support/bug-list/bug/CMS-49431) – Fixed an issue where block properties inside nested blocks did not save correctly.
*   [CMS-51656](https://world.optimizely.com/support/bug-list/bug/CMS-51656) – Fixed an issue where blocks in multisite setups returned `null` for `_metadata.url.base` and `_metadata.url.default` in Optimizely Graph responses, making it impossible to filter blocks by site.
*   [CMS-51841](https://world.optimizely.com/support/bug-list/bug/CMS-51841) – Fixed an issue where field labels and help text used different localization providers, causing inconsistent translations between captions and help text.
*   [CMS-51935](https://world.optimizely.com/support/bug-list/bug/CMS-51935) – Fixed an issue where the content tree returned a 400 error in certain admin plugins due to an antiforgery token timing problem.
*   [CMS-52030](https://world.optimizely.com/support/bug-list/bug/CMS-52030) – Fixed an issue where user synchronization failed when the synchronized users table contained `NULL` values in the `Email` or `GivenName` columns.
*   [CMS-52100](https://world.optimizely.com/support/bug-list/bug/CMS-52100) – Fixed an issue where converting a block property to a non-block property left orphaned data in the database, which could cause warnings about mismatched property definitions.
*   [CMS-52436](https://world.optimizely.com/support/bug-list/bug/CMS-52436) – Fixed an issue where pages with deeply nested block list properties caused Visual Builder to fail to load due to an excessively large metadata response.
*   [CMS-52661](https://world.optimizely.com/support/bug-list/bug/CMS-52661) – Fixed an issue where content type inheritance silently dropped inherited types when circular references existed among content type definitions, causing missing contracts, properties, or schema entries.

## June 4[](#h_01KTC1MK8B672BEJ02C8NB02Z9)

#### Connect your AI client to CMS (SaaS)

The [CMS (SaaS) MCP server](https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/mcp-server-overview) is now available, letting developers use AI tools like Claude with full CMS context to accelerate front-end development and CMS-connected workflows. Generate components, model content, and run CMS operations using natural language grounded in your real CMS structure and data.

After you [configure the MCP server](https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/configure-mcp-server), you can ask questions like _What content types were updated in the last year?_ or _Create a page using this design file_ and get real results from your CMS instance.

The MCP server lets you do the following:

*   **Generate front-end components** – Create CMS-ready front-end components using AI tools based on your content types.
*   **Model content** – Define CMS content types and contracts through natural language.
*   **Configure live preview** – Set up or troubleshoot live preview workflows in React applications.
*   **Set up the JavaScript SDK** – Configure the CMS JavaScript SDK in new projects.
*   **Run bulk content operations** – Perform bulk CMS content operations through AI-assisted workflows.
*   **Build reporting workflows** – Create CMS reporting workflows joined with external data sources.

#### Control when your environments receive platform updates

CMS (SaaS) platform releases now roll out progressively through [ring deployments](https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/overview-saas#platform-updates), replacing the previous all-at-once global deployment approach. Each release advances through controlled groups of accounts, called rings, only after passing validation, limiting the impact of potential issues before they reach production. 

Assign different projects or environments to different rings to match your team's needs. For example, keep production in the **Main** ring for maximum stability, and move staging to the **Early Adopter** ring for advance access to new features and early validation. 

Contact [Optimizely support](mailto:support@optimizely.com) to change your ring assignment.

## May 21[](#h_01KT4J89SSV0V6ZYSVA59H7E82)

#### (Beta) Manage Optimizely Graph search without developer help

(Beta) Released the [Optimizely Graph Search Management Portal](https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/platform-optimizely/docs/search-management-portal), a dedicated UI that lets content editors and marketers configure search behavior directly, without developer involvement for day-to-day tasks. Find the portal in the Optimizely global navigation bar. The portal includes:

*   **Overview dashboard** – Shows total query volume, click-through rate, and problematic queries (those with low or no click-through), so you can spot where search is underperforming. Refreshes on demand and supports date-range filtering.
*   **Pinned Results** – Promotes selected content to the top of search results for chosen queries. Create, edit, and delete rules in the portal, and changes take effect immediately. (Formerly Best Bets in Search & Navigation.)
*   **Synonyms** – Expands query matching by defining term relationships, supporting two-way (equivalent) and one-way (directional) synonyms. Changes take effect within minutes.

Access requires Opti ID and Admin Center permissions for your Graph tenant. Pinned Results and Synonyms also require a one-time developer configuration. Use the in-portal feedback link to share feedback during the beta.

## May 18[](#h_01KTY9SSR0B3MEESNRWTXE830A)

#### Configure global fallback languages

Define a default [fallback language](https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/languages#add-a-language) at the instance level so visitors always see content in a supported language, even when a translation is not yet available. Global fallback languages are now available in the CMS UI under **Settings > Languages**.

#### Rebuild Optimizely Graph indexes without downtime

[Smooth rebuild](https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/smooth-rebuild) is now enabled for CMS (SaaS). Use **Settings > Smooth Rebuild** to build a new Graph index in the background while the current one stays live. When the rebuild is complete, review the new index, then promote it or revert to the previous state.

This follows a blue-green deployment strategy: a new slot receives a full content sync in the background while the current slot continues serving queries. After verifying the new slot, accept it to swap instantly or abandon it to keep the current data unchanged.

#### Map content with flexible property types

[Content type binding property mappings](https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/manage-content-type-bindings-using-the-rest-api#create-a-content-type-binding) are now more flexible. Property types with fewer capabilities automatically map to types with more capabilities, reducing the need to modify existing content types when working with external content or content type bindings.

The expanded mappings include:

*   **Text properties** – `ShortString` maps to `LongString`, `XhtmlString`, `LinkItem`, or `URL`. `LongString` maps to `XhtmlString`, `LinkItem`, or `URL`.
*   **Number properties** – `Integer` maps to `Decimal`, `ShortString`, `LongString`, or `XhtmlString`. `Decimal` maps to `ShortString`, `LongString`, or `XhtmlString`.
*   **Content reference properties** – `ContentReference` maps to `LinkItem` or `URL`. Typed content references (`ContentReference<T>`) map to untyped `ContentReference`, `LinkItem`, or `URL`.

## January 27[](#opal-tools-and-agents)

#### Manage CMS content directly from Opal

Five new [Opal system tools for CMS](https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/39682866313613) let you create, update, publish, delete, and retrieve CMS content without leaving the Opal interface. All tools support all base content types, including pages, blocks, components, and media.

*   `cms_create_content_item` – Create a new empty draft content instance based on an existing content type. Specify a language branch, an optional container, and an initial collection of properties. You must manually publish drafts in the CMS UI.
*   `cms_update_content_item` – Update property values on a content item using its content key, version, and language. If the current version is published, a new draft is created automatically; if a draft already exists, it is updated. Also supports updating the outline for an Experience. This tool uses the Preview3 API.
*   `cms_publish_content_item` – Publish a specific content instance programmatically. Specify the language branch and an optional container.
*   `cms_delete_content_item` – Move a specific content instance to recoverable trash. Accepts the content item's ID and an optional language branch.
*   `cms_get_content_data` – Retrieve content data for a specific content item. Include a `ContentVersion` to retrieve a specific version, or omit it to retrieve the published version.
